query: Let `F : Schemeᵒᵖ ⥤ Type v` be a Zariski sheaf. Then for any small index type `ι`, `F` preserves limits of shape `Discrete ι` — i.e. `F` carries arbitrary coproducts of schemes to products of types.

    14  # The 1-hypercover of a glue data
    15  
    16  In this file, given `D : Scheme.GlueData`, we construct a 1-hypercover
    17  `D.openHypercover` of the scheme `D.glued` in the big Zariski site.
    18  We use this 1-hypercover in order to define a constructor `D.sheafValGluedMk`
    19  for sections over `D.glued` of a sheaf of types over the big Zariski site.
    20  
    21  ## Notes
    22  
    23  This contribution was created as part of the AIM workshop
    24  "Formalizing algebraic geometry" in June 2024.
    25  
    26  -/
    27  
    28  @[expose] public section
    29  
    30  universe v u
    31  
    32  open CategoryTheory Opposite Limits
    33  
    34  namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.GlueData
    35  
    36  variable (D : Scheme.GlueData.{u})
    37  
    38  /-- The 1-hypercover of `D.glued` in the big Zariski site that is given by the
    39  open cover `D.U` from the glue data `D`.
    40  The "covering of the intersection of two such open subsets" is the trivial
    41  covering given by `D.V`. -/

    44    I₀ := D.J
    45    X := D.U
    46    f := D.ι
    47    I₁ _ _ := PUnit

    49    p₁ i₁ i₂ _ := D.f i₁ i₂
    50    p₂ i₁ i₂ _ := D.t i₁ i₂ ≫ D.f i₂ i₁
    51    w i₁ i₂ _ := by simp only [Category.assoc, Scheme.GlueData.glue_condition]

    58      refine zariskiTopology.superset_covering (fun T g _ ↦ ?_) (zariskiTopology.top_mem _)

    14  # Sheaves preserve products
    15  
    16  We prove that a presheaf which satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to certain presieves
    17  preserve "the corresponding products".
    18  
    19  ## Main results
    20  
    21  More precisely, given a presheaf `F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type*`, we have:
    22  
    23  * If `F` satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to the empty sieve on the initial object of `C`,
    24    then `F` preserves terminal objects.
    25    See `preservesTerminalOfIsSheafForEmpty`.
    26  
    27  * If `F` furthermore satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to the presieve consisting of the
    28    inclusion arrows in a coproduct in `C`, then `F` preserves the corresponding product.
    29    See `preservesProductOfIsSheafFor`.
    30  
    31  * If `F` preserves a product, then it satisfies the sheaf condition with respect to the
    32    corresponding presieve of arrows.
    33    See `isSheafFor_of_preservesProduct`.
    34  -/
